plan.title: Crohn's ileum: DE + hallmark signature scoring per sample
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 ileum samples (6 Crohn-disease inflamed vs 6 control), raw gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), unpaired, single batch. Sample sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. Per the retrieved procedure, this flag is kept and inspected rather than silently dropped: it is carried through QC and only removed with a stated reason if it proves to be a genuine outlier on PCA/sample-distance grounds, not for depth alone (R-0008/R-0030). The research question asks for a per-sample score for every hallmark signature and which signatures differ between inflamed and control — this is the sample_scores enrichment case, for which GSVA + limma-on-scores is the grounded method (R-0102/R-0133), using the 50 MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets staged in the reference store. UCell rank-based per-sample scores are added as a complementary, depth-robust scoring method (rank-based scores do not depend on sample sequencing depth, useful given the shallow sample), each signature tested with limma/t-test on the score matrix with BH correction across the 50 signatures. A standard DESeq2 Wald + apeglm differential expression analysis anchors the gene-level result and supplies the ranked statistic that motivates and cross-validates the pathway-level signal. Track T1 does DE, T2 does GSVA/hallmark enrichment, T3 does UCell scoring, and a final report step integrates all three with explicit treatment of the low-depth sample.

Combined DE + GSVA hallmark score report
